name: Buprenorphine
drug_class: Opioid partial agonist (mu partial agonist, kappa antagonist)
route_note: Sublingual tablets and films (alone or with naloxone) for opioid use disorder; weekly/monthly subcutaneous depots; transdermal patches and buccal film for pain; injection; formerly an implant.

discovery.by: John Lewis and colleagues, Reckitt & Colman, Hull
discovery.note: A thebaine-derived oripavine developed in a search for a potent analgesic with low abuse potential.

rx_status: controlled (US Schedule III; UK Class C, Schedule 3)
tagline: Partial opioid agonist central to treatment of opioid use disorder
summary: Buprenorphine is a semi-synthetic partial mu-opioid agonist used for opioid use disorder and for pain. Its ceiling effect on respiratory depression and long receptor binding make it safer than full agonists, and it is a WHO essential medicine for opioid dependence.
mechanism: Buprenorphine binds mu-opioid receptors with very high affinity and slow dissociation but only partial intrinsic activity. It suppresses withdrawal and craving while producing a ceiling on euphoria and respiratory depression when used alone.

Because it displaces full agonists, it can precipitate withdrawal in people physically dependent on other opioids if started too early. It is also a kappa-opioid antagonist. Naloxone is added to sublingual products to deter injection, as naloxone is poorly absorbed sublingually but active if injected.
uses: Opioid use disorder (maintenance and withdrawal management)

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Reckitt & Colman chemists synthesise buprenorphine from thebaine.

history.title: Analgesic launch
history.detail: Temgesic injection is launched in the UK.

history.title: France
history.detail: France allows general practitioners to prescribe high-dose buprenorphine (Subutex) for opioid dependence, contributing to falling overdose deaths.

history.title: US approval for addiction
history.detail: The FDA approves Subutex and Suboxone; the 2000 DATA Act allows certified physicians to prescribe them in office settings.

history.title: Transdermal patch
history.detail: Butrans is approved in the US for chronic pain.

history.title: Monthly depot
history.detail: The FDA approves Sublocade, an extended-release subcutaneous injection.

history.title: Indivior settlement
history.detail: Indivior and its former parent Reckitt Benckiser pay large settlements over Suboxone marketing; Indivior pleads guilty in 2020.

history.title: X-waiver eliminated
history.detail: US law removes the special DEA waiver required to prescribe buprenorphine for opioid use disorder; Brixadi weekly and monthly depots are approved.

pk.metabolism: hepatic, CYP3A4 to norbuprenorphine and glucuronidation

serious: Respiratory depression, especially with benzodiazepines or alcohol
safety.boxed_warning: Sublocade/Brixadi: serious harm or death if injected intravenously (risk of occlusion and thromboembolic events), so they are only available through restricted programmes. Pain products carry the opioid class boxed warning.

facts: Buprenorphine for opioid use disorder is on the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines alongside methadone.
Buprenorphine can be prescribed in office-based settings in the US, unlike methadone for addiction, which must be dispensed through certified opioid treatment programmes.
